1.explanation:
All of the pipeline‐proposal plumbing lives in these three files:

• src/language-js/options.js  defines and validates the `pipelineProposal` CLI/API option (names, default, allowed values).
• src/language-js/parser-babel.js  actually injects Babel’s `pipelineOperator` plugin into @babel/parser — it must take the user’s `pipelineProposal` option (`minimal`, `smart`, `fsharp`) and pass it into the plugin configuration.
• src/common/internal-plugins.js  is where built-in syntax plugins (like `@babel/plugin-syntax-pipeline-operator`) are resolved and loaded; it currently doesn’t propagate the proposal setting when instantiating the plugin.

Because none of these files correctly wires the `smart` (or the planned `fsharp`) proposal into the parser, the `#` placeholder is never recognized and triggers a syntax error. Fixing this requires updating the option definitions to include `smart`/`fsharp`, and then passing that option into the plugin instantiation in both the internal‐plugin loader and the Babel parser setup.
1.bug_scenario:
When formatting JavaScript that uses the “smart” pipeline‐operator proposal (the `#` placeholder) Prettier throws a syntax error on the `#` token. For example, running

  5 |> # * 2

with

  pipelineProposal: "smart"

ends up as:

  SyntaxError: Unexpected character '#' (1:6)

Minimal pipeline (`5 |> double`) still works, but the code that wires up Babel’s pipelineOperator plugin is only handling the default (minimal) proposal and never passes the `smart` or upcoming `fsharp` option through.

2.explanation:
1. src/language-js/options.js defines the language-specific option list for JavaScript, including pipelineProposal. It needs to declare and document ‘smart’ as a valid choice. 
2. src/language-js/parser-babel.js is where Prettier calls @babel/parser with plugins. It currently only passes pipelineProposal: "minimal" (or default) for the pipelineOperator plugin – it must be extended to forward pipelineProposal: "smart" (and later "fsharp"). 
3. src/main/options-normalizer.js enforces and normalizes the shape of options. It needs to include "smart" in the allowed enum for pipelineProposal so that option parsing and validation will accept it without error.
2.bug_scenario: In Prettier v1.17.1 the “smart” pipeline-operator proposal (“5 |> # * 2”) isn’t recognized. When you pass pipelineProposal: "smart" to prettier.format, the Babel parser still isn’t configured to accept the “#” placeholder and throws SyntaxError on the “#” token. Only the “minimal” proposal (no placeholder) works today, but the code paths for recognizing and passing “smart” haven’t been wired up.
